summary: The narrator, a fugitive who has been drinking to steady herself, is confronted in a parking lot by two security guards after they catch her with a half-drunk bottle and suspect underage drinking. A bystander recognizes her as the 'psycho from the paper' accused of killing many people, the crowd grows, sirens sound, and the guards back away. The narrator flees by leaping up a display of potted plants onto the roof and running off the back of the building.
one_line: A fugitive narrator, mistaken for a mass murderer, escapes security guards and a gathering crowd by leaping onto a building roof.
key_facts: The narrator had self-medicated enough to stabilize her world for the moment.
The narrator considered going back to the Chinatown apartment to check for an ID hidden in her stash in the drywall.
The two security guards detained the narrator on suspicion of underage drinking after seeing her half-drunk bottle on the ground.
The narrator said, "I swear I'm over twenty-one," and offered to leave.
The female security guard pulled out a walkie and told the narrator to stay where she was.
The narrator carried an illegal Ruger tucked in the back of her belt and grenades in her pockets.
A dark-skinned, curly-haired woman shrieked, "The psycho from the paper! You caught her!"
The male guard said, "She does look like it," after taking in the narrator's features.
The guards began backing away, deeming their rent-a-cop duties not worth risking their lives against a homicidal maniac.
The narrator heard sirens starting up from not too far away.
Some onlookers pulled their children away, and at least two people pulled out mobile phones.
The narrator spun and leapt, running up a display of potted plants against the wall like stairs.
The narrator cleared the eaves in a dive and rolled back to her feet on the flat rooftop.
Shouts erupted behind the narrator as she ran across the roof and launched herself off its back.
